title: Is the Lovecraftian layer smart or does it feel like a cop-out?
author: Aromatic-Being5180
selftext:
Hi! I've been building a small browser game and I'd love honest feedback, both on the design and on whether it's fun.

**The concept** You're the new border officer at the Arrivals gate of Caldera, a sunny island republic that works like a tax haven. The UN is putting pressure on the island, so from today checks get stricter and new rules arrive day by day. Every passenger in the queue is an LLM character. You type whatever you want, check their papers, search their luggage, call hotels or relatives to verify their story, read the archives, and then stamp: ADMITTED, DENIED or DETAINED. It also works as online co-op: up to 3 players walking around the same office (booth, computer, phone).

**How the AI is used**

* Each passenger has a hidden character sheet (who they are, what they hide, how they lie). A cheap, small model plays them; the key stays server-side.
* Replies are structured: text + facial expression. Emotions have some inertia, so a single line doesn't flip the mood; key moments still can.
* Characters don't volunteer their story. Liars want in at all costs: first proof → an excuse invented in their own style, second different proof → a half-truth, the core fact only when they're really cornered.
* Phone calls (including prank calls and a very persistent coffee-machine salesman) and office emails are also generated live.

**The part I'm least sure about** Small models slip: they blank on details, especially about their private life. Instead of fighting every slip with more prompt rules, I made it part of the lore. On Caldera people suffer from "the long season": memory lapses that the local paper reports on, and something old in the sea behind it all. When a traveller blanks on a detail, the screen ripples for a moment with a faint sound, and there's a bigger Lovecraftian omen during the day. The idea: turn the model's weak spot into a creepy breadcrumb instead of an immersion break.

**My questions**

1. Does the AI interrogation feel convincing? Where does it break for you?
2. Is using a Lovecraftian layer to "justify" LLM slips a smart design move, or does it feel like a cop-out?
3. And simply: do you like it? What would make you play a second day?

Free in the browser, English & Italian, no sign-up:

[https://valico-di-grest.github.io/border-pass-int/varco/](https://valico-di-grest.github.io/border-pass-int/varco/)

itch.io: [https://dporto.itch.io/grest-frontier](https://dporto.itch.io/grest-frontier)

Thanks, I'll read every comment!
